title: Selected attention MatMul integrated with MNN
update: Report-confirmed: TinyViT runs with /layers.3/blocks.1/attn/MatMul_output_0 offloaded to Jerry’s 16×16 array. Inputs [1,10,49,32] × [1,10,32,49] use 320 padded 16×16×16 PIO jobs; reduction tiles are accumulated on the CPU. The final full-SoC image runs at 80 MHz. Two synthetic inputs completed; six physical matrix smoke cases passed. Single-run end-to-end timings were 5.74% faster for zeros and 2.71% slower for nonuniform input, so consistent speedup and dataset accuracy remain unproven. Next: repeated matched CPU/offload runs, overhead profiling, real-image numerical checks, then evaluate additional offloads. Implementation-plan ownership also includes design alternatives and the Jan–Feb matched MNN baseline.

title: USB camera setup and HPS-only live classification
update:
USB camera and HPS-only live classification (Nov 17, 2026)

- Completed USB camera peripheral setup on the DE1-SoC and verified live image capture through Linux/UVC.
- Created a live image-classification demo with TinyViT inference running on the HPS CPU, displaying the camera feed and predicted ImageNet class labels on the connected computer.
- Added a recording of the earlier CPU-only inference demo to ECE496 Files & Data. That recording uses Windows preprocessing; it does not document the subsequent HPS-local preprocessing work.

Next steps
- Integrate all team members’ software and FPGA hardware code to run end-to-end live image classification on the hybrid CPU–FPGA design, keeping image capture and preprocessing on HPS.
- Build and validate a timing measurement tool to separate capture/decode, preprocessing, CPU inference, FPGA computation, HPS–FPGA transfer/control, and result-display overhead. Record per-frame measurements and end-to-end latency to identify bottlenecks and compare the HPS-only and hybrid pipelines under matched settings.

title: Weekly update — SIMD, softmax and GELU
update:
- SIMD: On the Cortex-A9, 32×32 int8 matmul took 94.67 µs with NEON versus 202.12 µs in plain C (2.13× faster), with matching results. Used GCC -O3, 1,000 warmups and 10,000 timed runs.
- Softmax: Implemented 16-bit fixed-point softmax for up to 196 values using 33-cycle unsigned restoring division. All 147 rows / 8,666 outputs matched Python exactly; standalone timing passed 90 MHz using 222 ALMs and 10 M10Ks. Next: matmul integration and full-system testing.
- GELU: Bias + GELU is connected to accel_top’s CPU output-read path, processing 16 int8 lanes with a 256-byte bias buffer. Standalone timing passes 90 MHz; logic usage fell from 1,707 to 957 ALMs.
